scenes.narration: War is genuinely terrible. And yet, time after time, stock markets tend to rise right through the middle of it.
The uncomfortable reason is that the market measures corporate profit. It does not measure human suffering.
In theory, prices simply reflect all of the available information about future profit.
And war mobilizes an entire economy toward furious, around-the-clock production.
World War Two spending is what finally ended the Great Depression. US unemployment fell to around two percent.
And defense today is an eight hundred billion dollar a year industry.
The market is just counting profit, not morality. Does that honestly sit right with you?
